the majority of pediatric liver transplant recipients with operationally tolerant status maintained allograft histological stability over a 5‐year period.
we have shown that pediatric recipients of living donor liver graft who are tolerant to immunosuppression have stable liver histology in the absence of IS and have stable liver function tests.
we found no evidence that the liver allograft was damaged by the humoral allo‐immunity that was observed in the majority of subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a very forgiving organ.
operationally tolerant liver recipients can have a very stable clinical course over the long term, despite the presence of de novo donor-specific antibodies.
the liver allograft may be more resistant to chronic injury caused by alloantibodies than other solid organs.
